title: 실전모의 1회 142번: The Truth About Flights Over Antarctica
fullPassage: Have you ever wondered why commercial aeroplanes don't fly over Antarctica? It would, after all, be the most direct route from South Africa to New Zealand, or from Sydney to Buenos Aires — if the earth were round. But some conspiracy theories claim it isn't. According to these theories, there is no such thing as the south pole, so flying over Antarctica wouldn't make any sense. Plus, the Antarctic Treaty, signed by the world's most powerful countries, bans any flights over it because something weird is going on there. Well, in fact, some commercial routes do fly over part of the continent of Antarctica. The reason none overfly the South Pole itself is because of aviation rules that require any aircraft taking such a route to have expensive survival equipment for all passengers on board — which would obviously be prohibitive for a passenger jet. Most of Antarctica is out of the range that regulations specify for how far away an aircraft may fly from any emergency-landing airport.
